groups.problem: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of the owning userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens.
groups.rationale: All four point at the same lines and describe the same wrong-argument bug with the same fix.

groups.problem: Google Calendar stores the whole safeParse result ({success, data}) as the credential key instead of its data.
groups.rationale: Same lines, same wrapper-persisted bug, same fix of using .data.

groups.problem: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses stringified Zod schemas as computed keys, so it doesn't match arbitrary fields, and expiry and other token fields get stripped.
groups.rationale: All describe the broken computed-key schema that drops expiry fields. S11 frames it as a mismatch with the comment, but the root cause and fix are the same.

groups.problem: parseRefreshTokenResponse fills in the literal 'refresh_token' when the response has none, which overwrites the valid stored refresh token.
groups.rationale: Same lines and the same fabricated-token problem.

groups.problem: The sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Google, Zoho and HubSpot callers expect a different shape.
groups.rationale: All point at the same lines and describe the same response-shape mismatch with the same normalization fix.
